problem: The visually marked wing-tip and trailing-edge regions expose an opaque gray card perimeter. The exact source material controlling those pixels must be identified before any alpha correction is promoted.

actions: match clicked material by stateSetID, id, uid or name
record click screen position and material identifiers

alphaAuditModes.description: Reuse the selected material's existing AlbedoPBR, DiffusePBR or DiffuseColor texture object in the Opacity channel. This is the first test because the source RGBA texture may already contain a useful alpha channel that was not enabled.
Apply a generated RGBA mask only as a channel/UV diagnostic. It is not final unless its UV layout is proven to match the selected source material.

For the commercial-safe independent asset, author an alpha mask against the actual feather atlas UVs, with transparent voids, opaque vane core, narrow semi-transparent barb fringe, RGB dilation and alpha-aware mip levels.

prohibitedConclusions: A generated generic feather mask is not proof that the source atlas UVs are correct.
Enabling global opacity factor is not a feather-edge solution.
A whole material becoming translucent is a failure, not a pass.
Material-name matching alone is not enough; click evidence from the marked geometry is required.
